system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

Aiyana Brooks-Tan

Verdane Care
Re: Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) - Patient Experience
Dear Hiring Team,
Your Patient Experience role brings together three areas represented in my work: React
accessibility, booking websites and applications built with TypeScript and Node.js. I am
applying with professional frontend experience, a First Class Honours degree in Computing -
Software Development and practical examples relevant to Verdane Care’s patient-facing
features.
During my internship at Harbourline Media, I fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit
across more than 20 React components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and
ARIA labels. I also built a reusable image gallery component with Storybook stories and
wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library. This experience is directly relevant to
your emphasis on accessible React components and automated testing. My accessibility
knowledge is grounded in WCAG 2.1; your WCAG 2.2 AA standard provides a clear
benchmark for the role.
In my freelance work, I built a Next.js and Tailwind CSS booking website for a yoga studio,
hosted on Vercel. My final-year project, Tidewatch, was an accessible tide and weather app
for sea swimmers built with React, TypeScript and Node.js. Alongside my Express and
PostgreSQL skills, these projects provide a foundation for contributing beyond the frontend.
The booking project also offers a practical connection to Verdane Care’s appointment-booking
product, without equating that work with healthcare software experience.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my accessibility work, component testing and
booking-site experience could contribute to your Patient Experience squad. My portfolio and
GitHub links are included above. Thank you for considering my application.
Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
